sanskrit: vṛṣā vṛṣṇe duduhe dohasā divaḥ payāṁsi yahvo aditer adābhyaḥ | viśvaṁ sa veda varuṇo yathā dhiyā sa yajñiyo yajatu yajñiyām̐ ṛtūn ||
english: The bull-like one has milked out the milk-giving draughts of heaven for the bull-like one; the swift, inviolable son of Aditi. He knows all things even as Varuṇa knows through insight — let him, worthy of worship, perform sacrifice at the proper seasons.

sanskrit: rapad gandharīr apyā ca yoṣaṇā nadasya nāde pari pātu me manaḥ | iṣṭasya madhye aditir ni dhātu no bhrātā no jyeṣṭhaḥ prathamo vi vocati ||
english: May the Gandharva's consort and the water-maiden [Apsarās] guard my mind amid the roar of the stream. May Aditi establish us in the midst of the desired [realm]; our eldest brother, the foremost, shall proclaim it.

sanskrit: so cin nu bhadrā kṣumatī yaśasvaty uṣā uvāsa manave svarvatī | yad īm uśantam uśatām anu kratum agniṁ hotāraṁ vidathāya jījanan ||
english: Verily, glorious, splendid and luminous was the dawn that shone for Manu, rich in light. When the eager ones, following the will of the willing one, brought forth Agni as hotar for the assembly.

sanskrit: adha tyaṁ drapsaṁ vibhvaṁ vicakṣaṇaṁ vir ābharat iṣitaḥ śyeno adhvare | yadī viśo vṛṇate dasmam āryā agniṁ hotāram adha dhīr ajāyata ||
english: Then the falcon, impelled [by the gods], brought hither that far-reaching, all-seeing drop [of Soma] to the sacrifice. When the Āryan clans chose the wondrous Agni as their hotar, then was wisdom born.

sanskrit: sadāsi raṇvo yavaseva puṣyate hotrābhir agne manuṣaḥ svadhvaraḥ | viprasya vā yac chaśamāna ukthyaṁ vājaṁ sasavām̐ upayāsi bhūribhiḥ ||
english: Thou art ever joyful, O Agni, and flourishest like barley; the pious man's sacrifice proceeds well through thy priestly invocations. When the inspired sage, after his toil, brings thee the hymn-worthy praise, thou approachest [him] with abundant food-prizes won.

sanskrit: ud īraya pitarā jāra ā bhagam iyakṣati haryato hṛtta iṣyati | vivakti vahniḥ svapasyate makhas taviṣyate asuro vepate matī ||
english: The lover stirs up the two parents [Heaven and Earth] and desires to offer to Bhaga; the beloved one hastens, longing in his heart. The carrier [Agni] speaks, the active one is alert; the mighty asura [Agni] grows strong, trembling with inspired thought.

sanskrit: yas te agne sumatim marto akṣat sahasaḥ sūno ati sa pra śṛṇve | iṣaṁ dadhāno vahamāno aśvair ā sa dyumām̐ amavān bhūṣati dyūn ||
english: That mortal, O Agni, son of strength, who wins thy benevolence — he is heard beyond all others. Bearing food and borne along on horses, he, brilliant and mighty, adorns his days.

sanskrit: yad agna eṣā samitiḥ bhavāti devī deveṣu yajatā yajatra | ratnā ca yad vibhajāsi svadhāvo bhāgaṁ no atra vasumantaṁ vītāt ||
english: When, O Agni, this divine assembly gathers among the gods, worthy of worship, O worshipful one — and when thou distributest the treasures according to thy nature — may our share here be rich in wealth.

sanskrit: śrudhī no agne sadane sadhasthe yukṣvā ratham amṛtasya dravitnum | ā no vaha rodasī devaputre mākir devānām apa bhūr iha syāḥ ||
english: Hear us, O Agni, in the assembly, in the gathering-place; yoke thy chariot swift as the immortal. Bring hither to us Heaven and Earth, divine children; may thou never depart from the gods' company here.

sanskrit: dyāvā ha kṣāmā prathame ṛtenābhiśrāve bhavetaḥ satyavācā | devo yan martān yajathāya kṛṇvan sīdad dhotā pratyaṅ svam asuṁ yan ||
english: Heaven and Earth, the primal pair, are renowned through Order [ṛta] and are truthful of speech. When the god [Agni], making mortals ready for sacrifice, sat down as hotar, proceeding forward, guarding his own vital force.

sanskrit: devo devān paribhūr ṛtena vahā no havyam prathamaś cikitvān | dhūmaketuḥ samidhā bhārjīko mandro hotā nityo vācā yajīyān ||
english: The god who surpasses the gods through Order — first knowing all, bear our oblation. Smoke-bannered, blazing bright with fuel, the joyful hotar, eternal, most skilled in speech and sacrifice.

sanskrit: svāvṛg devasyāmṛtaṁ yadī gor ato jātāso dhārayanta urvī | viśve devā anu tat te yajur gur duhe yad enī divyaṁ ghṛtaṁ vāḥ ||
english: The divine immortal [Agni] is the self-yoker; when born from the cow [fire-sticks], they sustained the two broad [worlds]. All the gods followed after that sacrificial formula of thine when the bright [cow of heaven] milked out the divine ghee.

sanskrit: arcāmi vāṁ vardhāyāpo ghṛtasnū dyāvābhūmī śṛṇutaṁ rodasī me | ahā yad dyāvo asunītim ayan madhvā no atra pitarā śiśītām ||
english: I praise you two, O ghee-streaming waters, for your increase; O Heaven and Earth, O Rodasī — hear me. In the days when the heavens brought the vital breath's dispensation, may the two parents [Heaven and Earth] sharpen us here with sweetness.

sanskrit: kiṁ svin no rājā jagṛhe kad asyāti vrataṁ cakṛmā ko vi veda | mitraś cid dhi ṣmā juhurāṇo devāñ chloko na yātām api vājo asti ||
english: What has our king taken? In what have we transgressed his ordinance? Who knows fully? Even Mitra, though invoked, [may be] cheated among gods — yet may the call go forth; there still is prize-wealth.

sanskrit: durmantv atrāmṛtasya nāma salakṣmā yad viṣurūpā bhavāti | yamasya yo manavate sumantv agne tam ṛṣva pāhy aprayucchan ||
english: Here let him reconsider the name of the immortal [Agni] — that which, of equal mark, takes manifold forms. He who meditates well on Yama's [order] — protect him, O tall Agni, without ceasing in vigilance.

sanskrit: yasmin devā vidathe mādayante vivasvataḥ sadane dhārayante | sūrye jyotir adadhur māsy aktūn pari dyotaniṁ carato ajasrā ||
english: In whom the gods rejoice at the assembly, holding [their seats] in the dwelling of Vivasvat — in the sun they placed the light; in the moon the nights; the two luminaries circle unceasingly.

sanskrit: yasmin devā manmani saṁcaranty apīcye na vayam asya vidma | mitro no atrāditir anāgān savitā devo varuṇāya vocat ||
english: In that hidden thought wherein the gods wander together — we, for our part, know it not. May Mitra here [declare us] sinless, and Aditi; may divine Savitṛ speak to Varuṇa on our behalf.

sanskrit: śrudhī no agne sadane sadhasthe yukṣvā ratham amṛtasya dravitnum | ā no vaha rodasī devaputre mākir devānām apa bhūr iha syāḥ ||
english: Hear us, O Agni, in the assembly, in the gathering-place; yoke thy chariot swift as the immortal. Bring hither to us Heaven and Earth, divine children; may thou never depart from the gods' company here.

sanskrit: yuje vām brahma pūrvyaṁ namobhir vi śloka etu pathyeva sūreḥ | śṛṇvantu viśve amṛtasya putrā ā ye dhāmāni divyāni tasthuḥ ||
english: I yoke you two with the ancient sacred word, with reverences; may the hymn go forth like the sage's [chant] along its path. May all the sons of the immortal hear, even those who have taken up their stations in the divine realms.

sanskrit: yame iva yatamāne yad aitam pra vām bharan mānuṣā devayantaḥ | ā sīdataṁ svam u lokaṁ vidāne svāsasthe bhavetam indave naḥ ||
english: When you two came forth as the two striving [like a pair of twins], men devoted to the gods brought oblations to you. Take your own place, you who know it well — be a good seat for Indu [Soma] among us.

sanskrit: pañca padāni rupo anv arohaṁ catuṣpadīm anv emi vratena | akṣareṇa prati mima etām ṛtasya nābhāv adhi sam punāmi ||
english: I have mounted the five-footed [gāyatrī]; I follow the four-footed [triṣṭubh] according to sacred law. By the syllable I measure this [speech]; at the navel of Order [ṛta] I purify it together.

sanskrit: devebhyaḥ kam avṛṇīta mṛtyum prajāyai kam amṛtaṁ nāvṛṇīta | bṛhaspatiṁ yajñam akṛṇvata ṛṣim priyāṁ yamas tanvam prārirecīt ||
english: For the gods he [Yama] chose death; for progeny he did not choose immortality. They made Bṛhaspati the sacrificial ṛṣi; Yama yielded up his beloved body [to death].

sanskrit: sapta kṣaranti śiśave marutvate pitre putrāso apy avīvatann ṛtam | ubhe id asyobhayasya rājata ubhe yatete ubhayasya puṣyataḥ ||
english: The seven [streams] flow for the young Marut-accompanied one; the sons, for the father, have set Order [ṛta] in motion. Both [Heaven and Earth] reign over both aspects [of existence]; both strive and both nourish all.

sanskrit: pareyivāṁsam pravato mahīr anu bahubhyaḥ panthām anupaspaśānam | vaivasvataṁ saṁgamanaṁ janānāṁ yamaṁ rājānaṁ haviṣā duvasya ||
english: Honour with oblation Yama, the king, son of Vivasvat — who has gone forth along the mighty slopes, and has explored the path for many, the gathering-place of peoples.

sanskrit: yamo no gātum prathamo viveda naiṣā gavyūtir apabhartavā u | yatrā naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ pareyur enā jajñānāḥ pathyā anu svāḥ ||
english: Yama first discovered the way for us; this pasture cannot be taken away. Where our ancient Fathers went forth, there, born along that same path, all beings follow their own paths.

sanskrit: mātalī kavyair yamo aṅgirobhir bṛhaspatiḥ ṛkvabhir vāvṛdhānāḥ | yām̐ś ca devā vāvṛdhur ye ca devān svāhānye svadhayānye madanti ||
english: Mātalī grew strong with the Kavyas; Yama with the Aṅgirases; Bṛhaspati with those who chant the Ṛk. Those whom the gods exalted and those who exalted the gods — some rejoice with svāhā, others with svadhā.

sanskrit: imaṁ yama prastaram ā hi sīdāṅgirobhiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṁvidānaḥ | ā tvā mantrāḥ kaviśastā vahantu enā rājan haviṣā mādayasva ||
english: Come, O Yama, sit upon this sacred grass together with the Aṅgiras Fathers, in accord with them. May the seer-proclaimed mantras bring thee hither; with this oblation, O king, be gladdened.

sanskrit: aṅgirobhir ā gahi yajñiyebhir yama vairūpair iha mādayasva | vivasvantaṁ huve yaḥ pitā te 'smin yajñe barhiṣy ā niṣadya ||
english: Come hither, O Yama, with the Aṅgirases worthy of worship, of varied forms; rejoice here. I call Vivasvat, thy father — having sat down on the sacred grass at this sacrifice.

sanskrit: aṅgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāsaḥ | teṣāṁ vayaṁ sumatau yajñiyānām api bhadre saumanase syāma ||
english: The Aṅgirases are our Fathers — the nine-fold, the Atharvans, the Bhṛgus, the Soma-drinkers. May we abide in the good favour of those worthy of sacrifice, in their auspicious benevolence.

sanskrit: prehi prehi pathibhiḥ pūrvyebhir yatrā naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ pareyuḥ | ubhā rājānā svadhayā madantā yamam paśyāsi varuṇaṁ ca devam ||
english: Go forth, go forth on the ancient paths along which our ancient Fathers departed. There thou shalt behold the two kings rejoicing in the oblation — Yama and the god Varuṇa.

sanskrit: saṁ gacchasva pitṛbhiḥ saṁ yameneṣṭāpūrtena parame vyoman | hitvāyāvadyam punar astam ehi saṁ gacchasva tanvā suvarcāḥ ||
english: Unite with the Fathers, unite with Yama and with [the reward of] sacrifices performed and pious works, in the highest heaven. Leaving behind all imperfection, return again to home; unite with thy body, radiant.

sanskrit: apeta vīta vi ca sarpatāto 'smā etam pitaro lokam akran | ahobhir adbhir aktubhir vyaktaṁ yamo dadāty avasānam asmai ||
english: Depart, withdraw, and disperse from this [place] — the Fathers have made this world for him. With days, with waters, with nights illuminated — Yama bestows a resting-place upon him.

sanskrit: ati drava sārameyyau śvānau cataurakṣau śabalau sādhunā pathā | athā pitṝn suvidarāṁ upehi yamena ye sadhāmādam madanti ||
english: Run past the two dogs of Saramā, the four-eyed, brindled ones, by the good path. Then approach the gracious Fathers who feast together with Yama in joy.

sanskrit: yau te śvānau yama rakṣitārau cataurakṣau pathirakṣī nṛcakṣasau | tābhyām enaṁ pari dehi rājan svasti cāsmā anamīvaṁ ca dhehi ||
english: Thy two dogs, O Yama — the guardians, four-eyed, watchers of the road, observers of men — commit this man to their keeping, O king; grant him welfare and freedom from disease.

sanskrit: urūṇasāv asutṛpā udumbalau yamasya dūtau carato janām̐ anu | tāv asmabhyaṁ dṛśaye sūryāya punar dātām asum adyeha bhadram ||
english: Wide-nostrilled, life-drinking, fig-tree-coloured, the two messengers of Yama roam among men. May those two grant us today here to see the sun again — may they restore vital breath and blessings.

sanskrit: yamāya somaṁ sunuta yamāya juhutā haviḥ | yamaṁ ha yajño gacchaty agnidūto araṁkṛtaḥ ||
english: Press Soma for Yama, pour the oblation for Yama. The sacrifice goes to Yama, well-prepared, with Agni as its messenger.

sanskrit: yamāya ghṛtavad dhavir juhota pra ca tiṣṭhata | sa no deveṣv ā yamad dīrgham āyuḥ pra jīvase ||
english: Pour the ghee-rich oblation for Yama and step forward. May he bring us [the blessing] among the gods — long life for us to live.

sanskrit: yamāya madhimattamaṁ rājñe havyaṁ juhutana | idaṁ nama ṛṣibhyaḥ pūrvajebhyaḥ pūrvebhyaḥ pathikṛdbhyaḥ ||
english: Pour the sweetest oblation-offering for Yama the king. This homage [goes] to the ancient ṛṣis, the first-born, the first path-makers.

sanskrit: trikadrukebhiḥ patati ṣaḻ urvīr ekam id bṛhat | triṣṭub gāyatrī chandāṁsi sarvā tā yama āhitā ||
english: By the three Soma-pressings he [Yama] flies [encompasses] the six wide [worlds]; one alone is the Vast. Triṣṭubh, Gāyatrī — all the metres are established in Yama.

sanskrit: ud īratām avara ut parāsa un madhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ | asuṁ ya īyur avṛkā ṛtajñās te no 'vantu pitaro haveṣu ||
english: Let the lower Fathers rise up, and the higher, and the middle Soma-drinking Fathers. Those who have gone to life, the harmless, knowing Order — may those Fathers aid us at our invocations.

sanskrit: idam pitṛbhyo namo astv adya ye pūrvāso ya uparāsa īyuḥ | ye pārthive rajasy ā niṣattā ye vā nūnaṁ suvṛjanāsu vikṣu ||
english: Let there be homage today to the Fathers, those who departed first and those who departed later. Those settled in the earthly realm of dust, or those now among well-ordered communities.

sanskrit: āham pitṝn suvidarāṁ avitsi napātaṁ ca vikramaṇaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ | barhiṣado ye svadhayā sutasya bhajanta pitvas ta ihāgamiṣṭhāḥ ||
english: I have found the gracious Fathers, and Viṣṇu's grandson and his stride. Those who sit upon the sacred grass, who share by svadhā in the pressed [Soma] — may they come most swiftly here.

sanskrit: barhiṣadaḥ pitara ūty arvāg imā vo havyā cakṛmā juṣadhvam | ta ā gatāvasā śaṁtamenāthā naḥ śaṁ yor arapo dadhāta ||
english: O Fathers seated on the sacred grass, come hither to us with your help; enjoy these oblations we have made for you. Come with the most blessed aid; then grant us health and freedom from affliction.

sanskrit: upahūtāḥ pitaraḥ somyāso barhiṣyeṣu nidhiṣu priyeṣu | ta ā gamantu ta iha śruvantu adhi bruvantu te 'vantu asmān ||
english: The Soma-drinking Fathers have been called upon, at the dear sacred-grass resting places. Let them come, let them hear here; let them speak and protect us.

sanskrit: ācyā jānu dakṣiṇato niṣadyemaṁ yajñam abhi gṛṇīta viśve | mā hiṁsiṣṭa pitaraḥ kena cin no yad va āgaḥ puruṣatā karāma ||
english: Bending the right knee, sitting down, praise this sacrifice, all of you. O Fathers, harm us not for any sin that we, being but men, may have committed against you.

sanskrit: āsīnāso aruṇīnām upasthe rayiṁ dhatta dāśuṣe martyāya | putrebhyaḥ pitaras tasya vasvaḥ pra yacchata ta ihorjaṁ dadhāta ||
english: Sitting in the lap of the ruddy [dawn clouds], bestow wealth upon the mortal who gives. O Fathers, pass on to his sons the riches that are his; establish here for him vigour and strength.

sanskrit: ye naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ somyāso 'nūhire somapīthaṁ vasiṣṭhāḥ | tebhir yamaḥ saṁrarāṇo havīṁṣy uśann uśadbhiḥ pratikāmam attu ||
english: Those ancient Soma-drinking Fathers of ours, the most excellent, who followed the Soma-drinking [rite] — may Yama, rejoicing with them, eat the oblations at his pleasure, himself eager with the eager ones.

sanskrit: ye tātṛṣur devatrā jehamānā hotrāvidaḥ stomataṣṭāso arkaiḥ | āgne yāhi suvidarebhir arvāṅ satyaiḥ kavyaiḥ pitṛbhir gharmasadbhiḥ ||
english: Those who thirsted [for the divine], striving toward the gods, knowing the priestly arts, shaping hymns of praise with [sacred] songs — O Agni, come hither with the gracious [Fathers], with the true, wise, cauldron-seated Fathers.

sanskrit: ye satyāso havirādo haviṣpā indrena devaiḥ sarathaṁ dadhānāḥ | āgne yāhi sahasraṁ devavandaiḥ paraiḥ pūrvaiḥ pitṛbhir gharmasadbhiḥ ||
english: Those who are true, eaters of oblation, drinkers of oblation, riding the same chariot with Indra and the gods — O Agni, come with a thousand praised by the gods, with the later and the earlier Fathers seated at the cauldron.

sanskrit: agniṣvāttāḥ pitara eha gacchata sadaḥ-sadaḥ sadata supraṇītayaḥ | attā havīṁṣi prayatāni barhiṣy athā rayiṁ sarvavīraṁ dadhātana ||
english: O Fathers tasted by Agni, come hither; well-guided, take your seats at each seat. Eat the oblations offered on the sacred grass; then bestow upon us wealth with all heroes.

sanskrit: tvam agna īḻito jātavedo 'vāḍ ḍhavyāni surabhīṇi kṛtvī | prādāḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svadhayā te akṣann addhi tvaṁ deva prayatā havīṁṣi ||
english: Thou, O Agni, invoked as Jātavedas, having made the oblations fragrant, didst carry them [to the Fathers]. Thou gavest [them] to the Fathers by the svadhā [call]; they ate — do thou, O god, eat the presented oblations.

sanskrit: ye ceha pitaro ye ca neha yām̐ś ca vidma yām̐ u ca na pravidma | tvaṁ vettha yati te jātavedaḥ svadhābhir yajñaṁ sukṛtaṁ juṣasva ||
english: Those Fathers who are here and those who are not here, those whom we know and those whom we do not know — thou, O Jātavedas, knowest how many they are; enjoy the well-performed sacrifice with the svadhā-offerings.

sanskrit: ye agnidagdhā ye anagnidagdhā madhye divaḥ svadhayā mādayante | tebhiḥ svarāḻ asunītim etāṁ yathāvaśaṁ tanvaṁ kalpayasva ||
english: Those [Fathers] burned by Agni, those not burned by Agni, who rejoice in the midst of heaven with the svadhā oblation — with those, O self-ruling one, fashion this vital dispensation for the body according to [thy] will.

sanskrit: mainam agne vi daho mābhi śoco māsya tvacaṁ cikṣipo mā śarīram | yadā śṛtaṁ kṛṇavo jātavedo athem enaṁ pra hiṇutāt pitṛbhyaḥ ||
english: O Agni, do not burn him entirely, do not scorch him; do not consume his skin nor his body. When thou hast made him done [cooked], O Jātavedas, then send him forth to the Fathers.

sanskrit: śṛtaṁ yadā karasi jātavedo athem enaṁ pari dattāt pitṛbhyaḥ | yadā gacchāty asunītim etām athā devānāṁ vaśanīr bhavāti ||
english: When thou hast made him done, O Jātavedas, then hand him over all around to the Fathers. When he goes forth by this dispensation of vital breath, then he becomes subject to the will of the gods.

sanskrit: sūryaṁ cakṣur gacchatu vātam ātmā dyāṁ ca gaccha pṛthivīṁ ca dharmaṇā | apo vā gaccha yadi tatra te hitam oṣadhīṣu prati tiṣṭhā śarīraiḥ ||
english: May his eye go to the Sun, his breath to the Wind; let him go to the sky and to the earth according to cosmic law. Or go to the waters, if it be fitting for thee there — abide in the plants with [thy remaining] body-parts.

sanskrit: ajo bhāgas tapasā taṁ tapasva taṁ te śocis tapatu taṁ te arciḥ | yās te śivās tanvo jātavedas tābhir vahainaṁ sukṛtām u lokam ||
english: The unborn portion — consume it with thy heat; let thy glow heat it, let thy flame heat it. Those auspicious forms of thine, O Jātavedas — with those carry him to the world of the pious.

sanskrit: ava sṛja punar agne pitṛbhyo yas ta āhutaś carati svadhābhiḥ | āyur vasāna upa vetu śeṣaḥ saṁ gacchatāṁ tanvā jātavedaḥ ||
english: O Agni, release him back again to the Fathers — he who, offered to thee, wanders with svadhā-offerings. Clothed in life, may the remainder [of his vital parts] come near; may [he] unite with his body, O Jātavedas.

sanskrit: yat te kṛṣṇaḥ śakuna ātatoda pipīlaḥ sarpa uta vā śvāpadaḥ | agniṣ ṭad viśvād agadaṁ kṛṇotu somaś ca yo brāhmaṇām̐ āviveśa ||
english: That which a black bird has pecked at thee, or an ant, a serpent, or a wild beast — may Agni make all that wholly free of ill, and Soma who has entered into the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: agner varma pari gobhir vyayasva sam prorṇuṣva pīvasā medasā ca | net tvā dhṛṣṇur harasā jarhṛṣāṇo dadhṛg vidhakṣyan paryankhayāte ||
english: Wrap thyself around with a coat of mail from Agni; cover thyself all over with fat and marrow. Lest the bold one [Agni], fiercely blazing, seizing and meaning to burn thee, encircle thee.

sanskrit: imam agne camasam mā vi jihvaraḥ priyo devānām uta somyānām | eṣa yaś camaso devapānas tasmin devā amṛtā mādayante ||
english: O Agni, do not tip over this cup; it is dear to the gods and to the Soma-drinkers. This is the cup from which the gods drink — in it the immortal gods take delight.

sanskrit: kravyādam agnim pra hiṇomi dūraṁ yamarājño gacchatu ripravāhaḥ ||ihaivāyam itaro jātavedā devebhyo havyaṁ vahatu prajānan ||
english: I send the flesh-eating Agni far away; let him go to the realm of Yama, carrying the impurity. But let this other Agni, Jātavedas, carry the oblation to the gods here, knowing well [his task].

sanskrit: yo agniḥ kravyāt praviveśa vo gṛham imam paśyann itaraṁ jātavedasam | taṁ harāmi pitṛyajñāya devaṁ sa gharmam invāt parame sadhasthe ||
english: That Agni who, flesh-eating, has entered your house — beholding this other Jātavedas — that god I carry away for the Fathers' sacrifice; may he drive the cauldron in the highest dwelling.

sanskrit: yo agniḥ kravyavāhanaḥ pitṝn yakṣad ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | pred u havyāni vocati devebhyaś ca pitṛbhya ā ||
english: May the Agni who carries the flesh, who worships the Fathers, the increasers of Order — may he announce the oblations forthwith, both to the gods and to the Fathers.

sanskrit: uśantas tvā ni dhīmahy uśantaḥ sam idhīmahi | uśann uśata ā vaha pitṝn haviṣe attave ||
english: Desiring [this], we place thee [on the altar]; desiring [this], we kindle thee. Desiring it, bring the desiring Fathers hither to eat the oblation.

sanskrit: yaṁ tvam agne samadahas tam u nir vāpayā punaḥ | kiyāmbv atra rohatu pākadūrvā vyalkaśā ||
english: Him whom thou, O Agni, hast fully burned — do thou extinguish him again. Let young dūrvā grass and the spreading vyalkaśā plant spring up here.

sanskrit: śītike śītikāvati hlādike hlādikāvati | maṇḍūkyā su saṁgama imaṁ sv agniṁ harṣaya ||
english: O cool one, O cooling one; O refreshing one, O refresher — by the frog-spell [or: O Maṇḍūkā], rejoice and gladden this Agni well.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṁ kṛṇotītīdaṁ viśvaṁ bhuvanaṁ sam eti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ prepares the bridal for his daughter; at that, all this universe comes together. The mother of Yama, the great wife of Vivasvat, disappeared when she was being carried [in the bridal procession].

sanskrit: apāgūhann amṛtām martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇām adaduḥ vivasvate | utāśvināv abharat yat tad āsīd ajahād u dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ||
english: They concealed the immortal [Saraṇyū] from mortals; having made a woman of like appearance, they gave her to Vivasvat. Then what there was [of her] she bore to the two Aśvins; Saraṇyū abandoned the two twin children.

sanskrit: pūṣā vetaś cyāvayatu pra vidvān anaṣṭapaśur bhuvanas gopāḥ | sa tvaitebhyaḥ pari dadat pitṛbhyo 'gnir devebhyaḥ suvidariyebhyaḥ ||
english: May Pūṣan, knowing the way, drive thee forth from here — the guardian of the world, whose cattle are never lost. May he hand thee over to those Fathers, and Agni to those gods who know well [their duty].

sanskrit: āyur viśvāyuḥ pari pāsati tvā pūṣā tvā pātu prapanthe purastāt | yatrāsate sukṛto yatra te yayus tatra tvā devaḥ savitā dadhātu ||
english: Universal Life [Āyur] shall guard thee on every side; may Pūṣan guard thee before on the forward path. Where the pious sit, where they have gone — there may the god Savitṛ establish thee.

sanskrit: pūṣemā āśā anu veda sarvāḥ so asmām̐ abhayatamena neṣat | svastidā āghṛṇiḥ sarvavīro aprayucchan pura etu prajānan ||
english: Pūṣan knows all these quarters [of the sky]; may he lead us by the most fearless [path]. The giver of blessings, radiant, all-heroic, never stumbling, knowing well, let him go before.

sanskrit: prapanthe pathām ajaniṣṭa pūṣā prapanthe divaḥ prapanthe pṛthivyāḥ | ubhe abhi priyatame sadhasthe ā ca parā ca carati prajānan ||
english: Pūṣan was born on the forward path of paths, on the forward path of heaven, on the forward path of earth. Moving toward both most beloved resting-places — coming and going — he travels knowing [the way].

sanskrit: sarasvatīṁ devayanto havante sarasvatīm adhvare tāyamāne | sarasvatīṁ sukṛto ahvayanta sarasvatī dāśuṣe vāryaṁ dāt ||
english: The god-loving call upon Sarasvatī; at the sacrifice as it extends they [call upon] Sarasvatī. The pious invoked Sarasvatī — may Sarasvatī bestow the prize upon the worshipper.

sanskrit: sarasvati yā sarathaṁ yayātha svadhābhir devi pitṛbhir madantī | āsadyāsmin barhiṣi mādayasvānamīvā iṣa ā dhehy asme ||
english: O Sarasvatī, thou who hast ridden on the same chariot, O goddess, rejoicing with the Fathers by the svadhā-offerings — seated on this sacred grass, be gladdened; bestow upon us vigour free from disease.

sanskrit: sarasvatīṁ yām pitaro havante dakṣiṇā yajñam abhinakṣamāṇāḥ | sahasrārgham iḻo atra bhāgaṁ rāyas poṣaṁ yajamāneṣu dhehi ||
english: That Sarasvatī whom the Fathers call upon, approaching the sacrifice from the south — the share of Iḻā [worship] worth a thousand — bestow prosperity of wealth upon the sacrificers.

sanskrit: āpo asmān mātaraḥ śundhayantu ghṛtena no ghṛtapvaḥ punantu | viśvaṁ hi ripram pravahanti devīr ud id ābhyaḥ śucir ā pūta emi ||
english: May the Waters, our mothers, cleanse us; may the ghee-purifying ones purify us with ghee. For the divine [Waters] carry away all impurity — I rise up from them purified and clean.

sanskrit: drapsaś caskanda prathamām̐ anu dyūn imaṁ ca yonim anu yaś ca pūrvaḥ | samānaṁ yonim anu saṁcarantaṁ drapsaṁ juhomy anu sapta hotrāḥ ||
english: The drop [of Soma] flowed forth following the first days, and this womb, and the one that was before. I pour the drop that flows along following the common womb — the seven hotars following.

sanskrit: yas te drapsaḥ skandati yas te aṁśur bāhucyuto dhiṣaṇāyā upasthāt | adhvaryor vā pari vā yaḥ pavitrāt taṁ te juhomi manasā vaṣaṭkṛtam ||
english: Whatever drop of thine spills, whatever shoot falls from the arms, from the lap of the vessel-goddesses [dhiṣaṇā], or from the adhvaryu priests, or from the purifying filter — that I pour for thee, called forth with mind and vaṣaṭ.

sanskrit: yas te drapsaḥ skanno yas te aṁśur avaś ca yaḥ paraḥ srucā | ayaṁ devo bṛhaspatiḥ saṁ taṁ siñcatu rādhase ||
english: Whatever drop of thine has spilled, whatever shoot fell down or away from the ladle — may this god Bṛhaspati pour it together for bounty.

sanskrit: payasvatīr oṣadhayaḥ payasvan māmakaṁ vacaḥ | apām payasvad it payas tena mā saha śundhata ||
english: The plants are full of sap; let my speech be full of sap. Let the sap of the waters be full of sap — with that, purify me together.

sanskrit: param mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṁ yas te sva itaro devayānāt | cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṁ rīriṣo mota vīrān ||
english: O Death, depart by thine own other path that is different from the gods' road. I speak to thee who hast eyes and ears: do not harm our offspring and do not injure our heroes.

sanskrit: mṛtyoḥ padaṁ yopayanto yad aitam drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṁ dadhānāḥ | āpyāyamānāḥ prajayā dhanena śuddhāḥ pūtā bhavata yajñiyāsaḥ ||
english: Having come here wiping away the footprint of Death, establishing a longer span of life, growing prosperous with progeny and wealth — pure, cleansed, be ye worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: ime jīvā vi mṛtair āvavṛtrann abhūd bhadrā devahūtir no adya | prāñco agāma nṛtaye hasāya drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṁ dadhānāḥ ||
english: These living ones have turned away from the dead; our invocation of the gods this day has been auspicious. We have gone forth to the dance and to laughter, establishing a longer, further span of life.

sanskrit: imaṁ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṁ dadhāmi maiṣāṁ nu gād aparo artham etam | śataṁ jīvantu śaradaḥ purūcīr antar mṛtyuṁ dadhatām parvatena ||
english: I set this enclosing barrier for the living — may none of them proceed to that farther goal. Let them live a hundred autumns many-branching; may they hold Death within, as by a mountain.

sanskrit: yathāhāny anupūrvam bhavanti yatha ṛtava ṛtubhir yanti sādhu | yathā na pūrvam aparo jahāty evā dhātar āyūṁṣi kalpayaiṣām ||
english: As the days come in succession one after another, as the seasons go well in their proper order, as the later [season] does not abandon the earlier — so, O Creator [Dhātṛ], fashion for these ones their lifespans.

sanskrit: ā rohatāyur jarasaṁ vṛṇānā anupūrvaṁ yatamānā yati ṣṭha | iha tvaṣṭā sujanimā sajoṣā dīrgham āyuḥ karati jīvase vaḥ ||
english: Climb up to old age, choosing [long] life; go in order, striving, you who stand [here]. May Tvaṣṭṛ, well-born, of like mind, fashion for you here a long life to live.

sanskrit: imā nārīr avidhavāḥ supatnīr āñjanena sarpiṣā saṁ viśantu | anaśravo 'namīvāḥ sunatnā ā rohantu janayo yonim agre ||
english: These women here, not widows, blessed with good husbands — let them enter [the house] with collyrium and ghee. Tearless, free from affliction, adorned with fine jewels, let the wives first mount the [bridal] seat.

sanskrit: ud īrṣva nāry abhi jīvalokaṁ gatāsum etam upa śeṣa ehi | hastagrābhasya didhiṣos tavedam patyur janitvam abhi sam babhūtha ||
english: Rise up, O woman, to the world of the living; come, approach this one who lies here, lifeless. Thou hast fulfilled completely here the wifely state of him, thy husband, who took thy hand and desired thee.

sanskrit: dhanuṣ hastād ādadāno mṛtasyāsme kṣatrāya varcase balāya | atraiva tvam iha vayaṁ suvīrā viśvāḥ spṛdho abhimātīr jayema ||
english: Taking the bow from the hand of the dead man — for our lordship, brilliance, and strength — right here thou [shalt be] and here we, rich in heroes, shall conquer all enemies and those who hate us.

sanskrit: upa sarpa mātaram bhūmim etām uruvyacasam pṛthivīṁ suśevām | ūrṇamradā yuvatir dakṣiṇāvata eṣā tvā pātu nirṛter upasthāt ||
english: Creep to thy mother, this Earth, the wide-spreading, pleasant-abiding Earth. Young maiden, soft as wool, may she, who gives on the right side, protect thee from the lap of Nirṛti.

sanskrit: uc chvañcasva pṛthivi mā ni bādhathāḥ sūpāyanāsmai bhava sūpavañcanā | mātā putraṁ yathā sicābhy enam bhūma ūrṇuhi ||
english: Heave thyself up, O Earth; oppress him not. Be easy of access, easy to pass by, for him. As a mother wraps her son in her robe, so cover him, O Earth.

sanskrit: ucchvañcamānā pṛthivī su tiṣṭhatu sahasram mita upa hi śrayantām | te gṛhāso ghṛtaścuto bhavantu viśvāhāsmai śaraṇāḥ santv atra ||
english: Let the earth, heaving up, stand firm; let [the pillars] be propped up for a thousand [years]. Let those houses drip with ghee; let them be a refuge for him here for all days.

sanskrit: ut te stabhnāmi pṛthivīṁ tvat parīmaṁ logaṁ nidadhan mo ahaṁ riṣam | etāṁ sthūṇām pitaro dhārayantu te 'trā yamaḥ sādanā te minotu ||
english: I prop up the earth from thee [the corpse], placing this clod upon it; may I not be harmed. Let the Fathers hold fast this pillar; here may Yama fashion thee a seat.

sanskrit: pratīcīne mām ahanīṣvāḥ parṇam ivā dadhuḥ | pratīcīṁ jagrabhā vācam aśvaṁ raśanayā yathā ||
english: In the westward days they [the funeral priests] have laid me aside like a leaf. I have seized westward speech, as one seizes a horse by a rein.

sanskrit: ni vartadhvam mānu gātāsmān siṣakta revatīḥ | agnīṣomā punarvasū asme dhārayataṁ rayim ||
english: Turn back, do not go away; let the prosperous [cattle] cling to us. O Agni and Soma, ye who restore wealth — hold fast riches among us.

sanskrit: punar enā ni vartaya punar enā ny ā kuru | indra eṇā ni yacchatv agnir enā upājatu ||
english: Turn them back again, bring them back and settle them here. May Indra restrain them; may Agni drive them hither.

sanskrit: punar etā ni vartantām asmin puṣyantu gopatau | ihaivāgne ni dhāraye iha tiṣṭhatu yā rayiḥ ||
english: May these turn back again; may they thrive here with their herdsmen. O Agni, hold [them] fast right here; let the riches remain right here.

sanskrit: yan niyānaṁ nyayanaṁ saṁjñānaṁ yat parāyaṇam | āvartanaṁ nivartanaṁ yo gopā api taṁ huve ||
english: That [power] of leading forth, of bringing down, of agreement, of going away — the turning back, the returning — I call upon whoever is the guardian [of that power].

sanskrit: ya udānaḍ vyayanaṁ ya udānaṭ parāyaṇam | āvartanaṁ nivartanam api gopā ni vartatām ||
english: He who raised the dispersing, he who raised the going-away — may the guardian of the turning back and the returning now turn back.

sanskrit: ā nivarta ni vartaya punar na indra gā dehi | jīvābhir bhunajāmahai ||
english: Turn back, cause to turn back; O Indra, give us back our cows again. May we enjoy [them] while they are alive.

sanskrit: pari vo viśvato dadha ūrjā ghṛtena payasā | ye devāḥ ke ca yajñiyās te rayyā saṁ sṛjantu naḥ ||
english: I set [this charm] around you on every side with vigour, with ghee, with milk. Whatsoever gods are worthy of worship — may they join riches together with us.

sanskrit: ā nivartana vartaya ni nivartana vartaya | bhūmyāś catasraḥ pradiśas tābhya enā ni vartaya ||
english: O Turning-back, cause to turn; O Returning, cause to return. From the four quarters of the earth — from those, turn them [the cattle] back.

sanskrit: bhadraṁ no api vātaya manaḥ ||
english: Breathe upon us blessings of mind.

sanskrit: agnim īḻe bhujāṁ yaviṣṭhaṁ śāsā mitraṁ durdharītum | yasya dharman svar enīḥ saparyanti mātur ūdhaḥ ||
english: I praise Agni, youngest of those who enjoy [oblations], the friendly, hard-to-restrain one by [thy] command. In whose ordinance the bright cows [rays] attend the udder of their mother [the sky].

sanskrit: yam āsā kṛpanīḻam bhāsāketuṁ vardhayanti | bhrājate śreṇidan ||
english: Him whom the two lips nurture, shining with splendour as his banner — he blazes, bestowing brilliance in rows.

sanskrit: aryo viśāṁ gātur eti pra yad ānaḍ divo antān | kavir abhraṁ dīdyānaḥ ||
english: The lord goes forward on the path of the clans when he has reached the ends of heaven — the seer blazing through the clouds.

sanskrit: juṣad dhavyā mānuṣasyordhvas tasthāv ṛbhvā yajñe | minvan sadma pura eti ||
english: Enjoying the oblations of man, he has stood upright, mighty at the sacrifice — measuring out the seat, he goes forward.

sanskrit: sa hi kṣemo havir yajñaḥ śruṣṭīd asya gātur eti | agniṁ devā vāśīmantam ||
english: For he is the abode [of safety], the oblation, the sacrifice; by his hearkening [command] goes the path. The gods [seek] Agni with his chopper [vāśī].

sanskrit: yajñāsāham duva iṣe 'gnim pūrvasya śevasya | adreḥ sūnum āyum āhuḥ ||
english: I desire to serve [him] through the sacrifice of well-done worship — Agni of primal bliss. They call him the son of the rock, the living one [Āyu].

sanskrit: naro ye ke cāsmad ā viśvet te vāma ā syuḥ | agniṁ haviṣā vardhantaḥ ||
english: Whatever men come toward us from every side — may they all be good to us, magnifying Agni with oblation.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaḥ śveto 'ruṣo yāmo asya bradhna ṛjra uta śoṇo yaśasvān | hiraṇyarūpaṁ janitā jajāna ||
english: His course is black, white, ruddy; the tawny, the shining red, the glorious [are his colours]. The Creator [Janitā] has begotten him of golden form.

sanskrit: evā te agne vimado manīṣām ūrjo napād amṛtebhiḥ sajoṣāḥ | gira ā vakṣat sumatīr iyāna iṣam ūrjaṁ sukṣitiṁ viśvam ābhāḥ ||
english: Thus has Vimada [expressed] this insight for thee, O Agni, O son of vigour, in concord with the immortals. Seeking good favour, may he bring hither by song [the gifts of] food, vigour, good dwelling — thou who hast illumined all.
